record.original_question: For every family F of n pairwise disjoint closed line segments in the plane, must there exist a simple alternating path using at least on the order of log n input segments, where a simple alternating path is a nonintersecting polygonal chain that alternates between input segments from F and connecting segments, and the connecting segments are not allowed to intersect any other segment of F?

evidence.quote: A simple alternating path of F is a non intersecting polygonal chain
Conjecture 3 Any set F= {l1, . . . , ln} of n disjoint line segments has a simple alternating path with at least O(ln n) elements.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let F = {l_1, ..., l_n} be a family of n pairwise disjoint closed line segments in the Euclidean plane. A simple alternating path of F is a non-self-intersecting polygonal chain whose edges alternate between (i) "input edges," each of which is a segment of F, and (ii) "connecting edges," each of which has its two endpoints on segments of F and does not intersect any segment of F other than at those two endpoints. The length of such a path is the number of input edges (elements of F) it uses.

Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant c > 0 such that for every n and every family F of n pairwise disjoint closed line segments in the plane, F admits a simple alternating path that uses at least c · log n elements of F.
artifact.status_search_result: Hoffmann and Tóth proved that the segment endpoint visibility graph of any set of n pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane admits a non-crossing alternating path of length Ω(log n), confirming the conjecture; matching upper-bound constructions show the log n order is tight. Subsequent work ("Long Alternating Paths Exist," SoCG 2020) further extends results in this area.

status_evidence.title: Alternating Paths through Disjoint Line Segments (Hoffmann, Tóth)
status_evidence.snippet: Every segment endpoint visibility graph on n disjoint line segments admits an alternating path of length Ω(log n).
status_evidence.claim: Proves the Ω(log n) lower bound conjectured for alternating paths through disjoint segments.

status_evidence.snippet: Published version establishing the logarithmic lower bound.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the conjecture in a peer-reviewed journal.

status_evidence.title: Long Alternating Paths Exist (SoCG 2020)
status_evidence.snippet: Further work on long non-crossing alternating paths.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up research building on the resolved conjecture.
